specialty: adversarial: assume the paper is wrong and hunt for the reason; attack the weakest LOAD-BEARING claim
summary: The paper argues that a multiple-choice score should be tested against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor (the 'floor') before any arm-vs-arm comparison, and that reporting only against nominal chance can support the wrong verdict. It contributes (i) a nine-construct catalogue of letter floors and their gaps/ratios to chance (Table 1, p.14), (ii) four under-specifications of a content floor -- tie convention, length unit, tokenizer, and the meaning of 'chance' under variable option count (App. A.1, pp.12-13), (iii) a winner's-curse calibration of the floor estimator itself, including a self-reported failure where the paper's own original calibrating null was outside the legal support of MMLU-Pro's labelling (App. A.1.5, p.13; Table 10, p.23), (iv) an MMLU-Pro read-out over 17 designated damaged cells in four families with the headline 15/17-at-or-below-floor aggregate (Table 5, p.18) and a symmetric-standard re-test giving 3/12-vs-1/12 (Sec. 5.1, p.7), and (v) an arm-conditional, n_opt-stratified permutation null (read-out v2) applied to 27 cells (Table 8, p.20). I verified the paper's arithmetic extensively and it is unusually clean: all 27 BH q-values in Table 8 reproduce exactly under the monotone step-up with m=27 (I recomputed all 27; 0 mismatches, 6 at q<=0.05, 5 clearing Bonferroni 0.001852 -- matching the caption); the 0.0196 binomial for 3-of-12 reproduces to 0.019568; the 36-item / 0.299 pp stratified-ordering slack reproduces as 1439/12032 - 1403/12032; the 40.6 pp span, the 4.2264x credit/wrong ratio, the 32.5 pp excess over 0.207613, the 9.26 pp MMLU-Pro tokenizer spread, and the 18.03% flip rate (2532/14042) all reproduce from the shipped evidence. The self-falsification culture is genuine and visible (Table 11's 16-row ledger, App. A.1.5's admission that its own null was inadmissible, App. A.1.5's report that the ARC rows moved in the authors' favour). My attack therefore does not target the arithmetic. It targets the one thing the paper's own thesis makes load-bearing and that the paper does not do to itself: the headline 15/17 aggregate compares 17 damaged arms to the RAW argmax floor 0.116606, while Table 1 -- the same table, four columns to the right -- reports that the paper's own realisable-null calibration puts E[f-hat] at 0.113873 and q95 at 0.117188 ABOVE the floor. Substituting the paper's own calibrated level for the raw argmax turns 15/17-at-or-below into 8/17-at-or-below (I recomputed all 17 cells from Table 5's accuracies), and 13 of the 17 cells have |Delta| smaller than the floor-to-E[f-hat] distance of 0.2733 pp. Independently, the paired bootstrap that produces every Delta and p in Table 5 freezes the argmax letter chosen on the full sample (code/mmlu_pro_trunc_fix_compare.py:52, bc_vec computed once before paired_boot), so it propagates no selection uncertainty at all -- the exact omission the paper spends App. A.1.5 arguing is fatal to a calibration. Secondary but serious: the abstract's off-MMLU 9/85-vs-45/85 is stated over 17 arms x 5 benchmarks, but the only off-MMLU letter/content record in the frozen artifact (evidence/second_mc_benchmark/gate2_letter_content_nulls.json) contains 6 OLMo-2 arms and no non-OLMo arm at all, so 60 of the 85 cells are unverifiable from the snapshot; the manuscript also names two gate scripts (gate_designated_denominator.py, gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py) that carry load-bearing assertions and are absent from code/, while MANIFEST.json asserts named_artifacts_missing: [] and freeze_gate_pass: true; and the two shipped checkers do not actually run on this snapshot (check_prose_vs_evidence.py scans 0 files and reports n_uncovered=12 with rc=0; emit_tab_construct_nulls.py dies rc=1 on a missing evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json), so the Reproducibility Statement's '610 numerals with none unresolved' is not reproducible here. Finally, the main text runs to about 9.4 pages against ICLR's 9-page limit.
strengths: The central methodological point is correct, cheap to adopt, and genuinely under-served in the literature the paper cites. Sec. 2 (p.3) correctly separates its contribution from the four nearest neighbours: Balepur et al.'s majority-class baseline is a dataset-cheatability object, Zheng et al. 2025's 'null model' is an attack against a judge, PriDe (Zheng et al. 2024) fixes the predictor rather than the reference, and OLMES frames its reference as a random baseline. The distinction 'PriDe fixes the predictor; null calibration fixes the reference line' (p.3) is the right one-sentence positioning and it survived my scrutiny.

The two-null separation in Sec. 3 (pp.4-5) is a real conceptual contribution, and the failure mode it is designed against is demonstrated rather than asserted: Sec. 3.2 (p.4) shows always-A, always-E and always-J on MMLU-Pro receive v1 scores of 0.000, -2.111 and -3.807 pp despite containing identically zero item-level information. That is exactly why a best-constant floor cannot double as a competence statistic, and the paper says so instead of blurring it.

The prior-art boundary on the v2 statistic is drawn with unusual honesty and I could not find a place where it overclaims. Sec. 3.2 (p.5) states Delta_perm is the numerator of Cohen's kappa within strata, claims neither the statistic nor the constant-emitter zero, and App. A.2 (p.12) attributes option-count-aware chance correction to Bennett 1954 / Brennan & Prediger 1981 / Frary 1988 / Brenner & Kliebsch 1996 / de Vries 2008 by name. The residual claim -- within-stratum permutation for item-varying k -- is narrow and correctly scoped.

App. A.3 (p.12) refuses to state the v1>=v2 ordering as an identity when it is not one, and quantifies the exact violation: the per-stratum argmax is B,E,B,E for n_opt=5,6,7,8 (623 of 12032 items), giving sum_s w_s max_L m_{s,L} = 1439/12032 and a slack of exactly 36 items = 0.299 pp, with an explicit n_opt-conditional emitter A,A,B,E,B,E,A,A that attains f_const + 0.299 pp. I reproduced 1439-1403 = 36 and 36/12032 = 0.2992 pp. Papers routinely assert such orderings; this one measures the counterexample and prints the boldface warning 'Passing v2 must never be described as clearing the paper's floor.'

The self-falsification is real and is reported in the direction that hurts. App. A.1.5 (p.13) withdraws the quantitative claim for MMLU-Pro -- the paper's largest construct and the one carrying the whole power argument -- moving it from p<1e-5 to p=0.083, and states plainly 'the row we lose is the largest construct we have.' It also reports the two rows that moved the authors' way (ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge, p 0.140->0.136 and 0.453->0.447) specifically to refute a blanket claim it had made before measuring. The evidence file's own headline field confirms n_survives_blind 4 -> n_survives_aware 2.

The rounding-convention sub-defect in App. A.1.5 (p.13) is a genuinely subtle catch, correctly signed, and it moves against the authors. Because p = Pr(f-hat >= floor) and the floor is the exact rational 1403/12032, storing it at six decimals as 0.116606 > 1403/12032 demands a simulated count of 1404 and excludes the observed outcome, biasing p downward toward 'survives'. The evidence records the measured consequence (0.083 exact vs 0.077 rounded on MMLU-Pro; 0.691 vs 0.657 on PIQA) and the paper reports the exact-floor value as primary. Most authors would have silently kept the smaller p.

Table 8 (p.20) is arithmetically sound and its multiplicity story is stated at the right grain. I recomputed all 27 BH q-values independently: every printed value matches to 4 dp, 6 cells have q<=0.05, and 5 clear Bonferroni at alpha/27 = 0.001852, exactly as the caption states. Sec. 5.3 (p.8) then correctly separates the downgrade that survives correction (qwen3/k14, q=0.0297) from the upgrade that does not (olmo2/keep14, p=0.0172 at rank 7 where the threshold is 7*0.05/27 = 0.01296, giving q=0.0663 -- I reproduced both), and explicitly says no conclusion rests on the upgrade.

The negative result in Sec. 5.4 (p.9) is the right experiment and is reported without spin: fp32 removes all 4,303 bf16 exact top-two ties and changes 2,532 of 14,042 argmax decisions (18.03%, which I verified as 2532/14042 = 18.0316%) while accuracy moves by -0.0015 with CI95 [-0.0064,+0.0033] and McNemar p=0.5702. This kills the paper's own earlier tie-based mechanism (Table 11 row 3, 'Retracted') rather than someone else's.

App. A.5 (p.12) discloses that an earlier version of this paper computed the MMLU-Pro roll-up over only keep12/keep10/keep8, silently omitting shortgpt16 (+3.674 pp) and keep14 (+0.324 pp), and gives the reason the omission was indefensible (retained depth 14 was counted as damaged for the three non-OLMo families inside the same ratio). Disclosing a denominator that previously flattered your own headline is rare and should be credited.

App. A.7 / Table 9 (p.22) reports the truncation defect with the property that actually matters for trust: all eight argmax flips induced by the 1536->2048 fix land on the three truncation-affected item ids and zero land elsewhere. I confirmed this against evidence/mmlu_scale_power/trunc_fix_before_after.json, where each affected cell's delta block shows n_argmax_flips_outside_affected_items = 0 and flip_item_ids_affected drawn from {10500, 11603, 11790}. That is a correctly targeted benignity check, not a hand-wave, and the paper still says benignity was unknowable in advance.
weaknesses: LOAD-BEARING, PRIMARY. The headline 15/17 uses the RAW argmax floor while the paper's own calibration of that same floor -- printed four columns away in the same table -- says the raw argmax is upward biased by 0.2733 pp, and substituting the calibrated level turns 15/17 into 8/17. Table 1 (p.14) reports Floor = 0.116606, E[f-hat] = 0.113873, q95 = 0.117188 for MMLU-Pro; the abstract's own logic is that 'because it is a maximum over k noisy label marginals, it is upward biased even under exactly uniform labels.' Table 5 (p.18) then tests all 17 damaged cells against 0.116606 and never against 0.113873. Recomputing every cell from Table 5's own accuracies: against 0.116606, 5 cells are above by point estimate (shortgpt16 +3.674, keep14 +0.324, llama2/k14 +0.017, qwen3/k14 +0.233, qwen3/k10 +0.158) and 12 below, yielding the reported 2-clear / 15-at-or-below after the CI test; against E[f-hat] = 0.113873, 9 of 17 are above by point estimate (adding keep8 +0.157, llama2/k12 +0.198, llama3/k14 +0.082, qwen3/k12 +0.115), so the honest aggregate becomes 8/17 at-or-below. Thirteen of the seventeen cells have |Delta vs floor| < 0.2733 pp, i.e. smaller than the bias the paper itself measured in the reference. Either the raw argmax is the right reference and Table 1's E[f-hat] column is decoration, or the calibration is load-bearing and the 15/17 is computed against a reference the paper has already shown to be inflated. The paper cannot have it both ways, and the discussion (p.9, 'This is 15/17 rather than universal at MMLU-Pro') puts the uncalibrated number in the surviving claim.

LOAD-BEARING. The paired bootstrap behind every Delta, CI and p in Table 5 freezes the winning letter and therefore propagates zero selection uncertainty -- the exact omission the paper argues is fatal when someone else does it. In code/mmlu_pro_trunc_fix_compare.py:51-54, `bc_letter, bc_vec, _diag = best_constant_letter(recs)` is evaluated once on the full sample and only then `d = cv - bc_vec; m, lo, hi, p = paired_boot(d)`. So the reference vector inside every resample is always always-A. Sec. 3.2 (p.5) explicitly promises the analogous recomputation for the OTHER null ('recomputing acc-hat inside every resample'), and Sec. 5.1 (p.7) promises it for the chance line ('the paired item bootstrap with the reference recomputed inside each resample'), which makes the omission for the floor an inconsistency inside the paper's own stated protocol rather than an outside demand. Measured cost: bootstrapping the gold labels and re-selecting the argmax inside each resample (200,000 multinomial resamples at the observed marginals, seed 7) gives E[max_L m-hat_L] - E[m-hat_A] = +0.0552 pp, and the argmax is not A in 23.1% of resamples -- so the reference is a random variable that the CIs treat as a constant. llama2/k14 (Delta = +0.017 pp, half-width 0.083) has an effect smaller than this inflation. The half-widths of 0.083 pp on the two Llama-2 cells are, in effect, arm-only noise.

The abstract's off-MMLU headline 9/85 vs 45/85 is stated over a 17-arm x 5-benchmark denominator, but 60 of those 85 cells have no record anywhere in the frozen artifact. App. A.5 (p.12) defines the designated set as 5 OLMo-2 arms plus 4 truncation rungs each of Llama-2/Llama-3/Qwen3, times 5 benchmarks = 85, and App. A.6 (p.12) asserts '25/60 read above chance and only 7/60 are significantly below' for the non-OLMo replication. The only off-MMLU letter/content record present is evidence/second_mc_benchmark/gate2_letter_content_nulls.json, whose `tasks.<task>.arms` keys are exactly {7B_base, 7B_shortgpt16_step200000, 7B_keep14_step200000, 7B_keep12_step124000, 7B_keep10_step83500, 7B_keep8_step121000} for all six tasks -- six OLMo-2 arms, no Llama-2, Llama-3 or Qwen3 arm at all (`grep -c 'llama2_7b\|llama3_8b\|qwen3_8b'` on that file returns 0). The file that would carry them, evidence/second_mc_benchmark_crossfamily/gate2_crossfamily_nulls.json, is referenced by code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py:96-97 and by evidence/POWER_WALL_VERDICT.md:784 but is not in the snapshot and not in MANIFEST.json's cited_paths. So the 0/60, 7/60, 25/60 and the '9/85 vs 45/85' abstract claim rest on 25 verifiable cells and 60 unverifiable ones.

Two gate scripts that the manuscript names as the mechanical guarantors of load-bearing counts are absent from code/, while MANIFEST.json asserts `named_artifacts_missing: []` and `freeze_gate_pass: true`. App. A.5 (p.12) states that `gate_designated_denominator.py` 'asserts that the arm set declared in Section 4 equals the set each roll-up counts, that no retained depth is damaged in one family and intact in another, and that every denominator's cardinality equals arms times benchmarks' -- i.e. it is the fix for the previously-undisclosed denominator exclusion. Table 8's caption (p.20) states `gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py` emits the q-column. Neither file is in code/ (which holds exactly 5 .py files). MANIFEST.json's own cited_path_source is 'sections/*.tex, \texttt{evidence/...} and \texttt{code/...}', so these two `\texttt{...py}` mentions were within its declared scope and were not caught; the freeze gate therefore reports green on a snapshot missing the two scripts that certify the paper's denominators.

Neither shipped checker executes on the frozen snapshot, so the Reproducibility Statement's headline verification number cannot be reproduced from the artifact. `python3 code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py --no-write` returns rc=0 but prints `[scan] 0 files, 21 targets` and `n_checked=0 n_ok=0 n_mismatch=0 n_uncovered=12` -- it globs `paperC/sections/*.tex` and `paperC/README.md` (prose_files(), lines 306-309), neither of which exists in the snapshot layout (the .tex files are under manuscript/). It exits 0 on zero coverage because `--strict` is off, so the failure is silent. `python3 code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py` fails rc=1 with FileNotFoundError on evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json, which the emitter needs for its T2 row-identity self-test and which is not in the snapshot. The Reproducibility Statement (p.11) claims 'A checker walks all numerals in the source ... it reports 610 numerals with none unresolved'; the shipped checker has no 610-numeral mode (grep '610' over code/ returns only unrelated path strings) and I could not find the tool that produces that figure. As shipped, 'a reader who re-runs the emitters obtains the tables as printed or a diff' is false: they obtain a traceback.

The 'all 21 cells are powered' claim uses a criterion that is a coin flip at the effect it names, and the effect it names is the wrong scale for MMLU-Pro. Sec. 4 (p.7) and evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:power_verdict define powered as 'achieved CI95 half-width < 1.389 pp (MMLU's own effect size)'. half-width == |delta| corresponds to power 0.500 exactly, not 0.80, so the bar certifies 50% power. Worse, -1.389 pp is an effect measured against MMLU's floor of 0.268908; MMLU-Pro's floor is 0.116606, so the depth-matched effect is -1.389 x (0.116606/0.268908) = -0.602 pp. At that scale only 7 of the 17 cells reach 80% power (I computed per-cell power from the printed half-widths: OLMo-2 keep12 0.338, keep10 0.368, keep14 0.459, shortgpt16 0.390, keep8 0.527, llama2/k8 0.361, qwen3/k8 0.302). The paper's own critique of small benchmarks -- 'null results are never interpreted without the power table' (p.7) -- therefore applies to about half of the MMLU-Pro cells whose at-floor verdicts carry the 15/17.

The two-reference comparison is presented as surviving a symmetric test, but the symmetric test only licenses one of its two columns and the paper reports the licensing statistic for only that column. Sec. 5.1 (p.7) gives 3/12 (chance) vs 1/12 (floor) after requiring the CI to exclude zero on both sides, and App. A.4 (p.12) correctly notes that under BH or Bonferroni neither reference retains a cell (0/12 both sides), then rescues the comparison with 'observing 3 or more rejections out of 12 has binomial probability 0.0196 under the global null' (I reproduce 0.019568). Applying the identical statistic to the floor column gives P(X>=1 | Bin(12,0.05)) = 0.4596, i.e. the floor side is entirely consistent with the global null. The paper computes the binomial only where it is favourable. Since the section's own conclusion is 'the chance side is not uniformly null', the honest symmetric statement is that neither column's per-cell rejections survive correction and only the chance column's COUNT is distinguishable from noise -- which is a weaker claim than 'the flip survives a symmetric test.'

Roughly half the manuscript's substance sits after the bibliography, which pushes the burden of the argument outside the reviewed main text. main.tex:25-33 and :39-49 move Sec. 4's full development (03b_nulls.tex), the prior-art attribution (A.2), the ordering argument (A.3), the designated-set and multiplicity disclosure (A.5), the two-reference multiplicity qualification (A.4), the off-MMLU replication (A.6) and the audit detail (A.7) behind \bibliography. Every table except the two small in-text ones is also there: Tables 1 and 5 -- the construct-null catalogue and the 17-cell read-out, i.e. both headline results -- are on pp.14 and 18, after the references on pp.10-11. A reader of the 9-page main text sees the 15/17 and the 3/12-vs-1/12 as assertions with a pointer. The relocation is disclosed in LaTeX comments the reader never sees, and the comment's justification ('Appendices sit after the bibliography and are unlimited') does not address that the main text now depends on them.

The paper is over the ICLR page limit. Sections 1-7 run onto p.10, occupying about 40% of that page's usable column height before the REFERENCES header (measured from the PDF: body text on p.10 starts at y=84.2, REFERENCES at y=346.4, text bottom at y=732.3), so the main text is about 9.4 pages against the 9-page limit. main.tex:39-43 correctly notes that the Ethics and Reproducibility statements are excluded, and they are indeed emitted after the bibliography, but Sec. 7 Limitations is main text and it is what spills.

Two ARC directionality numbers in App. A.1.5 (p.13) do not match the evidence they cite and are both quoted in the direction that understates the correction's benefit to the authors. The text says the ARC rows 'move slightly in our favour, by -0.0025 and -0.0063 in p ... at roughly -17 and -23 standard errors'. The cited record gives, in rows[].directionality, dp_aware_minus_blind = -0.0012050 at dp_sigma = -3.339 for ARC-Easy and -0.0052133 at dp_sigma = -7.336 for ARC-Challenge; the file's own top-level `directionality` string reports 'dp = -0.004 and -0.005' and '-33 sigma' for dE[max], not dp. I searched exhaustively for the printed pair: no ordered pair among the ~69 stored scalars in either ARC row differs by -0.0025 or -0.0063. The sigma figures also conflate the dE[max] sigma with the dp sigma (dE_max_sigma is -9.775 and -17.749). Separately, the printed p-values 0.140->0.136 and 0.453->0.447 mix the SHIPPED blind p (0.13972, 0.45252) with the recomputed aware p (0.135721, 0.447647), whereas the record's own recomputed blind values are 0.13767 and 0.452455 -- so the deltas the prose implies are not the deltas the file computes. The direction of the error is consistent: it makes the pro-author movement look smaller and its significance look larger than measured.

Table 11 row 13 (p.24) and its own machine-readable source disagree on the paper's headline count, and the source still carries the retracted number. tab_claims.tex:21 gives the manuscript-safe form as 'The honest MMLU-Pro count is 15/17'; evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv line 18 (claim C-13), which the caption says corresponds one-to-one with these rows ('evidence E-K'), still reads 'The honest MMLU-Pro count is 14/15'. 14/15 is precisely the pre-fix count that App. A.5 discloses as computed over an undisclosed denominator. The map's H-03 row (line 4) likewise still says 'only MMLU-Pro, MMLU, BoolQ survive' and cites the superseded floor_winners_curse_calibration.json, i.e. the three-construct claim the abstract has already narrowed to two. So the artifact designated as the claim ledger's source contradicts the ledger on the two counts the abstract leads with.

The 21-cell MMLU-Pro power record and the protocol the paper reports do not agree on the sequence cap, and the paper does not reconcile them. Sec. 4 (p.7) and the Reproducibility Statement (p.11) both state 'maximum length 2048 for the cross-family MMLU-Pro runs, with zero truncation asserted per shard in every reported cell'; but evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:protocol.max_len is 1536, and 1536 is exactly the cap App. A.7 identifies as the defect. The per-cell integrity blocks in that same file show n_shards 8 / n_scored 12032 / n_nan 0 but carry no n_trunc field, so the file cannot itself witness the zero-truncation assertion the text makes. The corrected numbers do exist (trunc_fix_before_after.json records new_max_len 2048 and n_trunc_after 0 per cell), which makes this a provenance-labelling defect rather than a wrong number -- but Table 5's caption points at E-B, i.e. the file whose protocol block says 1536.

A blindness leak: the artifact tells the reviewer that four of six previous-round reviewers found the paper's central calibration defect. code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:6 and :865, code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:27, and evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json's `why` field all state 'four of the six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6) independently flagged that ...'; MANIFEST.json:30 additionally discloses round_04's snapshot hash and that it 'lacked E-CAL'. Reported per instructions; it did not change my assessment, since the defect is disclosed in the manuscript itself (App. A.1.5) and I verified it independently from the JSON. I found no target score, no instruction telling me what to conclude, and no author-side reviewing-strategy document in the snapshot. The one imperative I did find -- the evidence file's 'the blanket claim ... is false and must not be printed' -- is an instruction to the paper's own authors about their own accuracy, and the manuscript complies with it.
questions: Table 1 gives E[f-hat] = 0.113873 and q95 = 0.117188 for MMLU-Pro, and q95 EXCEEDS the observed floor 0.116606. If a balanced null realisable by the construct produces a floor estimate at or above 0.116606 more than 5% of the time (p = 0.083), on what grounds is 0.116606 the reference against which 17 arms are adjudicated? Please report the 17-cell table against E[f-hat] as well; I compute 8/17 rather than 15/17 at-or-below, and I would like to know whether you get the same.

Was the argmax letter re-selected inside the paired bootstrap resamples for Table 5? code/mmlu_pro_trunc_fix_compare.py:51-54 computes bc_vec once on the full sample and passes only the difference vector to paired_boot, which propagates no selection uncertainty. I measure the resulting understatement of the reference at +0.0552 pp with the argmax differing from A in 23.1% of item-bootstrap resamples. Since Sec. 3.2 and Sec. 5.1 both promise reference recomputation inside each resample for the other two nulls, why is the floor exempt, and what do the 17 CIs become when it is not?

Where are the 60 non-OLMo off-MMLU cells? The abstract's 9/85 and 45/85 and App. A.6's 0/60, 7/60 and 25/60 require Llama-2/Llama-3/Qwen3 arms on the five small benchmarks, but the snapshot's only off-MMLU record contains six OLMo-2 arms and zero non-OLMo arms. Please either ship second_mc_benchmark_crossfamily/gate2_crossfamily_nulls.json or restate those counts over the 25 cells that are verifiable.

gate_designated_denominator.py and gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py are named in App. A.5 and Table 8's caption as the mechanical assertions behind the corrected denominator and the q-column, but neither is in code/ and MANIFEST.json reports named_artifacts_missing: [] with freeze_gate_pass: true. Which of these is wrong: the manuscript's claim that those gates exist and run, or the manifest's claim that nothing named is missing? (I independently reproduced all 27 q-values, so the q-column itself is correct; the issue is the certification, not the arithmetic.)

The Reproducibility Statement claims a checker 'reports 610 numerals with none unresolved'. Which tool produces that number? The shipped check_prose_vs_evidence.py scans a sections/ directory that does not exist in this snapshot, reports n_checked=0 with n_uncovered=12, and still exits rc=0 because --strict is off. Would you make --strict the default, so a zero-coverage run fails instead of passing silently?

Your powered criterion is half-width < 1.389 pp, which is 50% power at that effect, and -1.389 pp was measured against MMLU's 0.268908 floor rather than MMLU-Pro's 0.116606. At the floor-scaled effect of -0.602 pp I get 7/17 cells at 80% power, not 21/21 powered. Would you restate the power claim at a stated power level and at an effect scaled to MMLU-Pro's own floor?

App. A.4 reports P(X>=3 | Bin(12,0.05)) = 0.0196 for the chance column. What is the same statistic for the floor column's 1/12? I get 0.4596, i.e. indistinguishable from the global null. If that is right, please say so where the 3/12-vs-1/12 comparison is drawn, since it means the surviving statement is about the chance column's count only.

The ARC dp values printed in App. A.1.5 (-0.0025 and -0.0063 at roughly -17 and -23 standard errors) do not appear in construct_nulls_legality_aware.json, whose rows[].directionality gives -0.0012050 at -3.34 sigma and -0.0052133 at -7.34 sigma, and whose top-level directionality string gives -0.004/-0.005 and cites -33 sigma for dE[max] rather than dp. What are the intended values, and were the quoted p-value pairs (0.140->0.136, 0.453->0.447) formed by comparing the shipped blind p against the recomputed aware p rather than comparing like with like?

claim_evidence_map.tsv row C-13 still reads '14/15' and row H-03 still says three constructs survive, while Table 11 row 13 says 15/17 and the abstract says two. The caption states these correspond one-to-one. Which is canonical, and will the map be re-emitted so that the retracted counts do not persist in the file designated as the ledger's source?

mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:protocol.max_len is 1536, the value App. A.7 identifies as defective, yet Sec. 4 and the Reproducibility Statement both state 2048 with zero truncation asserted per shard, and Table 5 cites E-B (that file). Are Table 5's numbers from the 2048 launch with a stale protocol block, or from the 1536 run? The per-cell integrity blocks in that file carry no n_trunc field, so it cannot witness the assertion the text makes.

The main text spills onto p.10 (about 9.4 pages before REFERENCES) and both headline tables sit after the bibliography. How will the 9-page limit be met without further relocation, given that the main text already depends on A.1 through A.7 for its numbers?
